stories.headline: Expert warns why Iran is taking bigger risks as war continues According to Adiri, the recent confrontations with Iran are shaping a new reality in the Middle East and forcing Israel to reexamine the limits of the campaign.
stories.summary: Iran is taking bigger risks in its confrontations with Israel, shaping a new reality in the Middle East. Recent exchanges of fire have raised concerns of a return to all-out war. Iranian authorities have expressed readiness for stronger military confrontation if necessary. Analysts say Iran's leaders are seeking to defend their Hezbollah allies in Lebanon and maintain the regional balance of power. Israel's initial attack was aimed at dismantling Iran's ability to develop nuclear weapons. The UN watchdog has not found evidence of a nuclear weapons program. The US is currently in discussions with Iran over a potential deal, with progress expected to take a few days. The situation is forcing Israel to reexamine the limits of its campaign, with experts warning that Israel cannot afford to fear friction when facing an adversary willing to take risks.

stories.headline: US and Iran engage in tit-for-tat strikes after Apache helicopter shot down Iran attacked US bases in Jordan and Bahrain, the latest salvo in tit-for-tat strikes with the United States after the downing of a US helicopter over the Strai
stories.summary: Iran attacked US bases in Jordan and Bahrain, retaliating against US strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz. The US strikes were in response to the downing of a US Apache helicopter on Monday. The US described its actions as a "proportional response", while Iran's IRGC called them "vicious". The exchange of strikes follows a ceasefire between Israel and Iran, which was broken when the two countries exchanged strikes. The US had attacked Iranian ports and islands, prompting Iran to claim that diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been damaged. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded to US threats, as tensions between the US and Iran continue to escalate. The situation remains volatile, with both sides engaging in tit-for-tat strikes and exchanging accusations.

stories.headline: Dogs used in rape of Palestinians in Israeli prisons, ‘followed officers' commands’: Disturbing report surfaces Some of the former prisoners who were sexually tortured despite claiming to have no knowledge of the Hamas-led attack gave their testimonies to a publication.
stories.summary: Former Palestinian prisoners have given testimonies of being sexually tortured, including being raped by dogs, in Israeli prisons. The allegations, documented by rights groups such as the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights and Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor, date back decades but appear to have increased since Israel's war on Gaza in October 2023. Prisoners reported being surrounded by soldiers and guard dogs, and being raped by the dogs with encouragement from handlers. The Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied the allegations, calling them "Hamas propaganda" and "blood libels." However, the UN, International Criminal Court judges, and special rapporteur Francesca Albanese have expressed concerns over the widespread and systematic use of rape and sexual torture by the Israeli army against Palestinians. Multiple former prisoners have shared detailed testimonies in a documentary investigation.

stories.headline: Pakistan launches manhunt for four PoK protesters after crackdown killing 19 kids, 7 pregnant women Pakistan News: Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) administration launched a search operation for four protesters and announced a bounty of Rs 1 crore for informati
stories.summary: Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) administration has launched a manhunt for four protesters, offering a Rs 1 crore bounty for information. The crackdown follows recent demonstrations that turned violent, resulting in the deaths of 19 children and 7 pregnant women. The Home Department of the PoK government has initiated legal proceedings against prominent figures, including Shaukat Nawaz Mir and Khawaja Mehran Arshad, on charges of sedition and anti-state activities. The Joint Action Committee for Kashmir (JAAC) leader, Shaukat Mir, has accused Pakistani forces of unleashing a massacre against protesters, claiming shoot-at-sight orders were issued in response to peaceful protests. The situation in PoK has drawn attention at the UN Human Rights Council, with concerns over the increasing crackdown and violent protests in the region.

stories.headline: Windows Central] Xbox fans rally against Shift Up for 'Stellar Blade' - which is now exclusively NOT on Xbox Series X|S
stories.summary: Xbox fans are expressing disappointment on Shift Up's social media platforms after learning that the action-adventure game Stellar Blade will not be available on Xbox Series X|S. Developed by Shift Up and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment, Stellar Blade is set to release in 2024. The game follows protagonist Eve as she fights to save humanity from an alien race. Although Shift Up has confirmed a Nintendo Switch release, there has been no announcement regarding an Xbox port. The developer has also announced a new title, Stellar Blade: Blood Rain, with a darker setting and a new protagonist, Evie, and will be self-publishing the game. The lack of an Xbox release announcement has sparked a backlash from Xbox fans, who are seeking clarification on the possibility of a port.

stories.headline: [The Sentinel - of this Land, for its People] Apple’s parental control enhancements to strengthen child privacy on devices: Analysts
stories.summary: Apple unveiled new child safety and parental control features at WWDC 2026, enhancing protections for children on its devices. The features enable age-appropriate protections, app controls, contact approvals, and communication safety tools. To set up parental controls, users must first establish Family Sharing and add their child's Apple Account to the family group. Analysts praised the move, citing its consistency with Apple's privacy-first approach, particularly as global regulatory scrutiny around children's online safety intensifies. The enhancements allow parents to manage app access, contacts, and content exposure for their children, strengthening Apple's commitment to user privacy amid rising online safety concerns. The updates are seen as a significant step in promoting child safety and digital well-being, aligning with Apple's focus on protecting user data and privacy.

stories.headline: [GSMArena.com] OnePlus 15 gains support for AirDrop via Quick Share
stories.summary: The OnePlus 15 has gained support for AirDrop via Google's Quick Share platform, allowing direct file transfers between the smartphone and Apple devices. This feature enables seamless transfers with iPhones and Macs. To access the functionality, users may only need to update Quick Share. The OnePlus 15 is currently the only supported OnePlus handset. With this update, users can transfer files directly to an iPhone, iPad, or Mac without requiring a cable, third-party app, or cloud upload. The rollout of AirDrop support via Quick Share to the OnePlus 15 extends the direct transfer capability that Google first launched for Pixel devices. This development makes cross-platform file transfers between Android and iPhone faster and more convenient. The update is now available for OnePlus 15 users, providing a more streamlined file-sharing experience.

stories.headline: [EFTM] ASUS ExpertBook Ultra Review: Redefining the Corporate Laptop
stories.summary: ASUS has released the ExpertBook Ultra, a corporate laptop featuring the Intel Core Ultra 9 processor and 32GB RAM. The device delivers smooth, sharp, and snappy performance, along with impressive battery life. Australian reviewers have praised the ASUS ExpertBook P5 for its security, reliability, and performance, making it a suitable choice for business use. Additionally, ASUS has showcased other laptops, including the ROG Flow Z13-KJP, a gaming laptop developed in collaboration with Hideo Kojima. This gaming laptop boasts a 16-inch QHD+ OLED display with a 240Hz refresh rate, ideal for gaming and creative tasks. The company continues to update its commercial product line, with more releases announced on its ASUS For Business Facebook page. The ExpertBook series is redefining the corporate laptop market with its powerful performance and reliable features.

stories.headline: The Guardian: Wednesday briefing: What to expect from a World Cup beset with controversy
stories.summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is set to begin on Thursday, amidst controversy surrounding its approach. Andrew Giuliani, head of the FIFA task force, met with host city executives and DHS officials on Wednesday to discuss preparations. President Donald Trump has also been involved in discussions, speaking at a meeting of the White House Task Force on the FIFA World Cup 2026. Despite the controversy, FIFA has faced little pushback. The tournament is expected to be one of the largest and most-watched sporting events in the world, with a vast archive of content available to stream for free on FIFA+. The event has garnered great expectations, but enthusiasm has been muted due to the surrounding controversy. The tournament will be covered extensively by news outlets, including The New York Times and The Guardian.

stories.headline: BBC: World Cup 2026: How Thomas Tuchel started his path to England manager from wild hip-hop parties
stories.summary: Thomas Tuchel, the current England national football team manager, is bidding to become the first foreign manager to win the World Cup. His journey to this position began in unexpected surroundings, working at the Radio Bar, a hotspot for Germany's hip-hop scene. The bar's former manager, Carlos Coelho, recalled its popularity in a 2008 interview. Tuchel was appointed England manager in October 2024 and prefers a flexible, structured style of play. His primary goal is to guide England to the World Cup title, despite facing challenging matches in Group L. With his 4-2-3-1 or 3-2-5 formation, Tuchel aims to build a highly competitive team. As the 2026 World Cup approaches, Tuchel's unique path to the England manager position has been highlighted, from his early days in the hip-hop scene to his current role leading the national team.

stories.headline: Punch Newspapers: Portugal Coach Praises Super Eagles Ahead of Friendly
stories.summary: Portugal head coach Roberto Martinez has described Nigeria's Super Eagles as a "demanding opponent" ahead of their international friendly on Wednesday, June 10. The match is part of both teams' preparations for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The Super Eagles, under coach Eric Chelle, will face a strong Portuguese team that includes players like Cristiano Ronaldo and Ruben Dias. Martinez has warned that the friendly will be a competitive match, and the outcome will not influence his starting lineup decisions. The Super Eagles have arrived in Portugal and are set to take on the European team in Leiria. The friendly match is an opportunity for both teams to test their strength and strategy ahead of the World Cup. Nigeria is looking to rebuild and improve under Chelle's guidance.

stories.headline: MarkerZone.com: John Tortorella did it again after the Vegas loss and it's instant gold
stories.summary: Vegas Golden Knights head coach John Tortorella had an outburst after a loss, with cameras capturing the incident. The loss occurred during the 2026 Stanley Cup Finals, where the Carolina Hurricanes tied the series 2-2. The game saw a disputed call, with referee Jean Hebert ruling no goal on the ice. Tortorella challenged the call, citing a loose puck in front of the goalie. The challenge was unsuccessful, and Tortorella's frustration boiled over in a post-game exchange with a reporter. The incident has drawn attention, with many discussing Tortorella's coaching style and the intense pressure of the Stanley Cup Finals. The series is now tied, setting up a crucial next game between the Golden Knights and the Hurricanes. Tortorella's comments and actions are under scrutiny as the series continues.

stories.headline: Trinamool MP Sushmita Dev Quits Party, Meets Himanta Biswa Sarma Trinamool MP Sushmita Dev Quits Party In Another Setback For Mamata Banerjee
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Sushmita Dev has resigned from the Rajya Sabha and quit the party, dealing another blow to Mamata Banerjee's leadership. Dev, daughter of former Assam Congress leader Santosh Mohan Dev, submitted her resignation to Vice President and Rajya Sabha Chairman CP Radhakrishnan, requesting it be accepted immediately. She is the second Trinamool Rajya Sabha MP to resign this month, following Sukhendu Sekhar Roy's exit on June 8. After resigning, Dev met Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma in New Delhi, fueling speculation about her potential entry into the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The resignation comes amid internal rebellion within the Trinamool Congress, with Dev's departure marking a significant setback for the party. Her meeting with Sarma has added momentum to rumors of her imminent joining of the BJP.

stories.headline: PM Modi surpasses Nehru's record of longest-serving elected PM; global leaders congratulate him
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has become India's longest-serving elected Prime Minister, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru's record. As of June 10, Modi has been in power for 4,399 days, earning the trust of the people through his leadership. With 12 years in power, he is the only non-Congress leader to complete two full terms. Modi has rewritten history, breaking Nehru's 62-year-old record. Global leaders have congratulated him on this achievement, recognizing his continuous service as the elected Prime Minister. This milestone marks a significant moment in India's political history, with Modi etching his name into the country's record books. His leadership has been acknowledged by world leaders, who have extended their congratulations to him on this historic achievement.

stories.headline: Order XII Rule 6 CPC | Suit Can Be Decreed On Admission Only If It's Clear, Unequivocal And Unconditional: Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of India has ruled that a decree under Order XII Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) can only be granted when there is a clear, unambiguous, and unconditional admission of liability by the defendant. The court emphasized that pleadings must be construed to determine if the admission is categorical and unequivocal, entitling the plaintiff to relief without requiring a trial. The decree is a discretionary remedy, and the admission must be of such nature that it leaves no doubt or ambiguity. The Supreme Court's decision clarifies the conditions under which a decree can be passed on admissions, ensuring that only clear and unequivocal admissions can lead to a decree under Order XII Rule 6 CPC. This ruling provides guidance on the interpretation of admissions in civil proceedings.

stories.headline: Kerala High Court upholds new KEAM 2026 rank list formula for equalising CBSE, ICSE and State Board marks
stories.summary: The Kerala High Court has dismissed petitions filed by CBSE students challenging the state government's new marks normalisation formula for engineering admissions under the KEAM 2026 prospectus. The petitioners argued that the new formula, introduced without scientific study or expert recommendation, disadvantaged CBSE candidates. The court upheld the state's new standardisation formula, which aims to ensure uniformity in evaluating marks from different boards, including CBSE, ICSE, and Kerala Board of Public Examinations. The new formula replaces the standardization system used since 2012. The court rejected the pleas challenging Clauses 1.4 and 9.7.4 of the 2026 prospectus, which introduced the new normalization process for calculating marks obtained in qualifying examinations to prepare the engineering rank list. The decision upholds the state government's new rank list formula for equalising marks from different boards.

stories.headline: [Times Now] Top US Experts Raise Alarm As Flesh-Eating Screwworm Return After 30 Years
stories.summary: The New World screwworm, a flesh-eating fly, has returned to the United States after 30 years. The parasitic pest preys on livestock and other animals, and its larvae feed on the tissue of warm-blooded mammals, including livestock, pets, and sometimes humans. Female screwworm flies lay their eggs in wounds or cavities, causing infestation. Experts are sounding the alarm about the possibility of the New World screwworm regaining a foothold in the US. The insects had been eradicated 60 years ago but have started to crawl northward again. While experts advise vigilance, they caution against panic. The return of the screwworm poses a threat to livestock and animal health, and prompt action is necessary to prevent its spread. US experts are closely monitoring the situation to prevent a potential outbreak.

stories.headline: [BBC News] World’s largest chipmaker does not rule out price rises as costs increase
stories.summary: NVIDIA Corporation, the world's largest chipmaker, has not ruled out potential price rises due to increasing costs. The company's stock is expected to rise 26.58% in the next 3 months, with a 90% probability of staying between $260.74 and an unspecified higher price. Analysts have set a consensus price target of $298.42, representing a 49.26% increase from the current price of $208.64. Over the past 5 years, NVIDIA's stock price has increased by 1099.37%. Projections from 59 analysts estimate an average 12-month price target of $298.42, with a high estimate of $500 and a low estimate of an unspecified amount. If the forecast is met, NVIDIA's stock would have rallied 52.45% from its price of $196.79 in just 52 weeks.

stories.headline: [Australian Financial Review] Senior banker reveals “intimate” China notes
stories.summary: A senior banker recently emailed colleagues about a "relatively intimate" meeting organized by GIC, Singapore's sovereign wealth fund. She was seated next to Lim Chow Kiat, the CEO of GIC, during the meeting. The term "intimate" in this context refers to the close and private nature of the gathering, rather than any personal relationship. The meeting was likely focused on discussing business and investment opportunities with China. The banker's proximity to the CEO suggests she may have gained valuable insights and connections during the event. The meeting was part of GIC's efforts to facilitate dialogue and cooperation between Singapore and China. The senior banker's account of the meeting provides a glimpse into the high-level discussions and relationships that shape international business and finance. The meeting's details and outcomes have not been fully disclosed.

stories.headline: [Simple Flying] The Real Reason Pilots Sometimes Fly A Longer Route On Purpose
stories.summary: Pilots and flight dispatchers often intentionally avoid the shortest geographical route for various reasons, prioritizing safety, fuel efficiency, and passenger comfort. The path of a long-haul jet may appear as a curve that deviates from a direct line on a flight tracking map. However, this curve is not unnecessary, as it takes into account atmospheric physics and other factors. Airlines may choose longer routes for efficiency or safety reasons, and sometimes due to regulatory requirements. The straight line between two points is often an illusion on a flat map, and pilots must consider real-world conditions when planning a flight. By taking a longer route, pilots can ensure a safer and more efficient journey, making every departure a calculated compromise between geometry and reality. This approach is a common practice in real-life airline operations.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty climb on buying in blue-chips Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty climbed in early trade, driven by buying in blue-chip stocks like Reliance Industries and ICICI Bank, alongside a nota
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty climbed in early trade on Wednesday, driven by buying in blue-chip stocks such as Reliance Industries and ICICI Bank. The 30-share BSE Sensex rallied 303.73 points to 74,222.49, while the 50-share NSE Nifty went up by 85.40 points to 23,327.50. The gains were also supported by cooling crude oil prices and mixed global market cues. The Indian equity markets opened higher, with the Sensex and Nifty 50 gaining on the back of strong buying in key stocks. The positive trend in the market was evident from the early deals, indicating a strong start to the trading session on Wednesday, June 10.

stories.headline: Why is market rising Sensex jumps 1,000 points in 2 days, Nifty crosses 23,400 3 key factors behind the surge Indian stock markets surged for a second consecutive session, with Sensex and Nifty crossing significant milestones
stories.summary: Indian stock markets surged for a second consecutive session, with the Sensex jumping 1,000 points in 2 days and the Nifty crossing 23,400. Despite escalating Iran-US tensions, the markets were supported by cooling oil prices and a decline in the AI rally in global markets. The Sensex rose over 500 points, with the Nifty crossing 23,250 amid global optimism. The Indian market had recently corrected and bounced back from the 22,000 level, with sentiment turning positive. The market witnessed broad-based buying, lifting the Sensex and Nifty 50 by over 1% each in intraday trade on Thursday. The surge was driven by three key factors, with the Nifty holding above the 23,000 level, indicating a positive trend in the Indian stock market. The market's resilience has led to significant milestones being crossed by the major indices.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today | Opening Bell: Sensex, Nifty Start Marginally Higher; FMCG And IT Stocks Lead - Is Dalal Street Gearing Up For A Bigger Move
stories.summary: The Indian stock market benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, started marginally higher, led by FMCG and IT stocks. The Sensex soared 939 points at close, while the Nifty ended above 23,400, with banks, FMCG, and auto stocks leading the gains. The market staged a sharp recovery after a significant crash earlier in the day, boosted by reports of the government planning to reduce taxes and remove caps on bond ownership. The Sensex gained 2,946.32 points or 3.95% to close at 77,562.90, while the Nifty gained 873.70 points or 3.78% to close at 23,997.35. The market's positive sentiment was also influenced by the announcement of the US-Iran ceasefire, resulting in a nearly 4% gain in the indices.

stories.headline: Stock Market LIVE: GIFT Nifty signals lower open; Asia mkts decline as US launches strikes at Iran Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates, June 10: The GIFT Nifty, an early indicator of the Nifty50's performance, was trading slightly lower, tracking negativ
stories.summary: The GIFT Nifty is trading slightly lower, indicating a potential decline in the Nifty50's performance, due to negative global cues. This follows Friday's session where the NSE Nifty 50 closed 50 points or 0.21% lower at 23,367, and the BSE Sensex fell 117 points or 0.16% to 74,243. The Aquaculture sector stocks rose 2.55% in market capitalisation on Friday. The recent US strikes on Iran have escalated regional tensions, causing oil prices to surge and impacting import-dependent economies like India. The conflict has lasted 100 days, exceeding initial expectations of a two to four week duration. Asian markets are also declining in response to the geopolitical developments, contributing to the negative sentiment in the Indian stock market. The surge in oil prices is expected to have a significant impact on India's economy.

stories.headline: Australian Billionaires’ Sigma Healthcare In Talks To Buy U.K.’s Boots In Deal Valued At $10 Billion
stories.summary: Sigma Healthcare is in talks to acquire UK-based health and beauty retailer Boots in a deal valued at $10 billion. Boots operates 3,776 retail stores across 11 countries, including Ireland, Mexico, and Thailand. The company's owner is discussing the potential sale with multiple parties, including Sigma and the billionaire Weston family. A successful acquisition would accelerate Sigma's international expansion plans. However, Sigma faces competition from Canada's Weston family, and the potential transaction's value could exceed $10 billion. Following confirmation of the discussions, Sigma's shares fell up to 5.5% to A$2.76. The Australian company is also exploring other opportunities, including a partnership with Greenlight to license the Chemist Warehouse brand and provide support to 22 stores in London. The deal's outcome is uncertain, with Sigma competing against other bidders for the UK retailer.

stories.headline: Hong Kong debt market heats up as Tencent, Swire raise US$5.2b in multi-currency deals
stories.summary: Hong Kong's debt market is surging, with Tencent Holdings and Swire Pacific raising over US$5.2 billion in fresh funding through multi-currency deals. The issuance underscores the city's growing role as an international bond hub. Tencent, China's tech champion, and Swire Pacific, one of the country's oldest conglomerates, led the fundraising efforts. The deals highlight the city's attractiveness to investors and its ability to facilitate large-scale capital raisings. The fundraising comes as Hong Kong's debt market continues to boom, with the city solidifying its position as a major financial center. The successful issuance of multi-currency bonds by prominent companies like Tencent and Swire Pacific is expected to further boost investor confidence in the market. The transactions were reported on June 10, 2026, and demonstrate the city's growing status as a key player in international finance.

stories.headline: Trustd Brings Know Your Carrier to Market as Freight Fraud Costs European Supply Chains Over €1bn
stories.summary: Trustd has launched Know Your Carrier (KYC), a web-based verification tool, to help shippers and 3PLs instantly assess the risk of carriers quoting for work. The tool provides a risk signal via email in seconds. This launch comes as cargo crime across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) has risen 438% in three years, with over 108,000 supply chain thefts recorded. The increased cargo crime has resulted in additional costs of over €1 billion to European supply chains. The KYC tool aims to mitigate these risks by enabling shippers and 3PLs to verify carriers quickly and efficiently, helping to prevent freight fraud and protect their supply chains. The launch of KYC is a response to the growing need for secure and reliable transportation solutions in the region.

stories.headline: Nigeria Logistics Market Attracts New Global Partnership CEVA Logistics and EFL Africa form a joint venture, CEVA EFL Limited, to expand operations and strengthen their presence in Nigeria's logistics market.
stories.summary: CEVA Logistics and EFL Africa have formed a joint venture, CEVA EFL Limited, to expand operations in Nigeria's logistics market. The partnership combines EFL Africa's local expertise and infrastructure with CEVA Logistics' global network and supply chain capabilities. This joint venture aims to strengthen their presence in one of West Africa's most important and rapidly growing logistics markets. CEVA EFL Limited will deliver integrated and customer-focused logistics solutions, leveraging CEVA's global network and EFL's strong local presence. The move is expected to drive significant value for Nigeria, fostering knowledge transfer to local employees and empowering EFL to accelerate its growth. The new entity will operate in Nigeria, providing a strategic platform for delivering logistics solutions and solidifying the companies' position in the region. This partnership brings a global logistics leader into the Nigerian market.

stories.headline: OpenAI joins AI giants, files for US public listing
stories.summary: OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, has confidentially filed for a US initial public offering, joining rival Anthropic in a push toward a stock market listing. The company, valued at $852 billion, hopes to raise billions in the highly anticipated public offering. OpenAI's filing comes as it appears to be losing its early leads with consumers and businesses to Google and Anthropic. The move is part of a larger trend of AI companies rushing to go public, with the IPO pipeline now worth around $3.6 trillion. Anthropic, which makes the Claude chatbot, announced its own plans to go public last week. Traders on prediction market platforms now see OpenAI as the favorite to go public before Anthropic, giving it an 83% chance of debuting on the public markets first.

stories.headline: OpenAI Calls For Global Oversight To Manage Advanced AI Development Risks
stories.summary: OpenAI is calling for global oversight to manage the risks associated with advanced artificial intelligence development. The company proposes the creation of a global body to monitor AI work and intervene when risks outweigh safeguards. OpenAI suggests that large AI developers should undergo annual independent audits to ensure compliance with safety requirements and report critical incidents. This plan differs from the recent White House order, which established a voluntary framework for evaluating AI systems' cybersecurity risks. OpenAI's proposal comes as its CEO, Sam Altman, meets with White House officials and lawmakers to discuss AI regulation. The company's top policy executive has emphasized the need for independent oversight, citing the growing risks associated with powerful AI models, and has suggested that the US and China should collaborate on establishing global safety rules for AI.

stories.headline: Perplexity Sticks To 2028 IPO Timeline As OpenAI, Anthropic Take Steps To Public Markets
stories.summary: Perplexity AI plans to go public in 2028, unaffected by the market reception of upcoming listings from rivals OpenAI and Anthropic. CEO Aravind Srinivas stated that the company's IPO timeline remains unchanged, regardless of the outcome of its competitors' public offerings. OpenAI has filed for an IPO, potentially seeking a valuation of nearly $1 trillion, while Anthropic's latest financing round valued the company at around $965 billion. The moves underscore growing competition among leading AI developers. Despite this, Perplexity is committed to its 2028 IPO target, with Srinivas indicating that the company's plans are independent of its rivals' actions. The decision reflects Perplexity's confidence in its own growth and development trajectory.

stories.headline: Donald Trump, Bernie Sanders and Sam Altman are all talking about public ownership in AI
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met with Senator Bernie Sanders to discuss public ownership in AI companies. Sanders had proposed a plan for the public to take a 50% ownership stake in AI companies, using their stock to create a public wealth fund. The meeting highlighted the tension between AI powerhouses and policymakers. Notably, President Donald Trump also expressed interest in the idea of public ownership in AI. When informed of Sanders' proposal, Trump pointed out similarities in their coalitions. The discussions come as AI companies face increasing scrutiny from policymakers, with Sanders' plan aiming to spread the fortune generated by AI through a public wealth fund. The meeting between Altman and Sanders marks a significant development in the debate over the role of AI in society and its potential impact on the economy.
